# X11 — A2A v1.0 in practice for a "bring your own assistant" bake-off

> Batch 2, route X11. Read first per instructions: `docs/research/external/X4-a2a-adk-phoenix-delta.md` (batch 1, 2026-10-08) and `TechnoMile Agentic Black Hat/docs/research/swarm/A2A.md` (2026-10-03). This report extends X4 rather than repeating it; X4's findings on A2A v1.0 spec shape, ADK version deltas, and Phoenix version deltas are taken as given and cited by reference where reused.

# X11: A2A v1.0 in practice for a "bring your own assistant" bake-off

## Q1. Minimal a2a-sdk 1.2.x Python server/client, Agent Card, structured data, auth, timeouts

**Agent Card shape (two different "v1.0" shapes found, unreconciled — see Contradictions #1).** The `a2a-python` proto (Context7, `/a2aproject/a2a-python`, `a2a_v0_3.proto`, 2026-10-08) defines `AgentCard{protocol_version, name, description, url, preferred_transport, additional_interfaces, provider, version, capabilities{streaming, push_notifications, extensions}, security_schemes, security, default_input_modes, default_output_modes, skills, supports_authenticated_extended_card, signatures, icon_url}`. **High confidence** — primary SDK source code, matches X4.

**Server/client pattern (Context7, `a2a-python` samples/`cli.py`, 2026-10-08).** Server: `create_agent_card_routes(agent_card, card_modifier=None, card_url="/.well-known/agent-card.json")` serves the card as a Starlette GET route. Client: `A2ACardResolver(httpx_client, base_url).get_agent_card()` fetches the card; `create_client(card, client_config=ClientConfig(...))` builds a client; `client.send_message(SendMessageRequest(message=Message(role=Role.ROLE_USER, message_id=uuid4(), parts=[Part(text=...)], task_id=..., context_id=...)))` sends, returning a stream iterated with `_handle_stream`. **High confidence** — official sample code, directly runnable.

**Timeout for "host calls a remote agent with a strict timeout."** `ClientConfig` (Context7, `a2a-python` `client.py`) has no timeout field of its own; timeout is set on the `httpx.AsyncClient` passed into `ClientConfig.httpx_client`, i.e., the host constructs `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(connect=..., read=..., write=..., pool=...))` and hands it to both `A2ACardResolver` and `create_client`. ADK's own REST tool layer uses exactly this pattern with `connect=10.0, read=600.0, write=600.0, pool=10.0` as its default (Context7, `adk-python` `rest_api_tool.py`) and catches `httpx.TimeoutException`, returning a structured error rather than crashing. **High confidence** for the mechanism (primary SDK code); the specific numeric defaults are ADK's REST-tool defaults, not A2A-client defaults, so the arena must set its own strict read timeout explicitly rather than trust a 600s default.

**Structured data parts for a coaching-response schema.** `Part` is `oneof{text, FilePart, DataPart}`; `DataPart{data: google.protobuf.Struct}` carries an arbitrary JSON object (Context7, `a2a-python` proto, 2026-10-08). This is the concrete carrier for AST-2/AST-3's flag+follow-up+finding+confidence object: build it as a Pydantic model server-side (ADK's `output_schema` on an `LlmAgent`, Context7 `adk.dev/agents/llm-agents/`, 2026-10-08), serialize to a `DataPart`, and have the host parse `DataPart.data` against the arena's own JSON Schema/Pydantic model before trusting it — **A2A validates nothing about the content; validation is entirely the host's responsibility**, true for both in-process and A2A-transported candidates. **High confidence** on the DataPart mechanism; **medium confidence** that ADK's `output_schema+tools` combination is reliable on the specific Gemini tier the arena will use — X4 already flagged an unreconciled contradiction here (Gemini-3.x-only vs. an unqualified `gemini-2.5-flash` example), still unresolved this session.

**Task states.** Confirmed unchanged from X4: `SUBMITTED, WORKING, COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELED/REJECTED (terminal), INPUT_REQUIRED/AUTH_REQUIRED (interrupted)`. The `AgentExecutor.execute()` docstring (Context7, `agent_executor.py`, 2026-10-08) draws the line explicitly: emit a single `Message` for an immediate response, or emit a `Task` plus streamed `TaskStatusUpdateEvent`/`TaskArtifactUpdateEvent` for long-running work. For a sub-3-second coaching turn, the single-`Message` immediate-response path is the natural fit; the Task/streaming path is for candidates that genuinely need more than one turn to settle. **High confidence.**

**Auth (API key, OAuth, mTLS).** `security_schemes` on the card can hold an `HTTPAuthSecurityScheme(scheme='bearer')` (Context7, `a2a-python` test fixture, 2026-10-08) — i.e., bearer-token/API-key-style auth is a first-class, documented pattern. New this session: ADK's `A2aRemoteAgentConfig` exposes `card_request_interceptors` (`CardRequestInterceptor`) and `request_interceptors` (`RequestInterceptor`) — async hooks that run "before the card is fetched" and "before each outgoing task request" respectively, letting the host attach a bearer token or arbitrary header per candidate (Context7, `adk-python` `docs/guides/a2a/agent/config/index.md`, 2026-10-08). This is the concrete mechanism for issuing each of the 3 assistant candidates its own API key in a bake-off. **No concrete mTLS code example surfaced** in any source reached this session (Context7 or GDK) — the spec's `SecurityScheme` model supports OAuth2-style schemes and HTTP auth schemes, but mTLS, if used, more likely lives below the SDK at the transport/ingress layer (Cloud Run's own TLS termination), not as an app-visible A2A construct. **Medium confidence on API-key/bearer, low confidence/open question on mTLS** — not found, not ruled out.

**Signed Agent Cards.** `AgentCard.signatures: repeated AgentCardSignature` exists in the proto (Context7, 2026-10-08). Per web search (2026-10-08, multiple sources including `towardsai.net` and `api7.ai` blog posts dated around the v1.0 release), v1.0's signed cards use JWS (RFC 7515) over JCS-canonicalized (RFC 8785) card content, letting a receiver verify a card was actually published by the domain it claims — directly relevant to verifying a bake-off entrant's card wasn't spoofed. **Medium confidence** — the field's existence is primary-sourced; the JWS/JCS mechanism description comes from secondary blog commentary, not the spec text itself, which this session did not fetch directly.

## Q2. Fairness, isolation, validation, conformance for an untrusted external agent

**A2A carries no native "equal budget" concept.** There is no token cap, spend cap, or fairness primitive anywhere in the Agent Card, Message, or Task schema retrieved this session. "Equal budgets" (BKO-5: consistent public tools, context limits, response budgets) must be enforced entirely at the arena's harness layer — same work whether a candidate runs in-process or over A2A: a wall-clock timeout (the `httpx.AsyncClient` timeout above), a turn-count cap enforced by the interviewer harness (mirrors TechnoMile's own non-A2A budget enforcement — see Q6), and truncation of what goes into the outbound packet. **High confidence** (absence-of-feature finding, corroborated by both the SDK schema and the TechnoMile precedent).

**Isolation (host sends only the public packet).** Nothing in A2A enforces this; it is a pure serialization-boundary discipline — a function that builds the outbound `Message`/`DataPart` from only SCN-7/SCN-8 fields, never SCN-9's evaluator-only packet, is required regardless of transport. **High confidence.**

**Output validation.** Same point as Q1: the host must parse whatever the candidate returns (a `DataPart` JSON object, or free text) against the arena's AST-7/AST-8 schema itself; a parse failure should be treated as "unsupported/unresolved" (EVL-5), not surfaced as a crash. **High confidence**, consistent across both GDK and Context7 sources.

**Conformance testing.** Two concrete tools exist: **a2a-inspector**, a browser tool that fetches the agent card, checks spec compliance, offers a live-chat test channel, and shows raw JSON-RPC 2.0 traffic in a debug console (GDK `answer_query`, 2026-10-08; corroborated by web search hits for `github.com/a2aproject/a2a-inspector` and multiple blog write-ups, 2026); and **`adk conformance test`**, which replays a `spec.yaml` + recorded baseline (`generated-recordings.yaml`, `generated-session.yaml`, with SSE variants) and can emit a Markdown report (GDK `answer_query`, 2026-10-08). Both are debugging/validation tools, not demonstrated as CI gates in any source reached. A TCK run "proves the wire contract holds... but leaves answer quality untested — a conformant agent can still invent policy or leak data" (`testmuai.com`, web search, 2026, undated specific day but indexed in 2026 results) — i.e., **conformance testing answers "is this a legal A2A agent," not "is this answer correct, schema-faithful, or honest,"** which is exactly the gap the arena's own scorer must fill. **Medium confidence** — official tool existence is high confidence; the "insufficient for answer quality" framing is a single secondary source, directionally obvious but not independently corroborated.

**Isolation for untrusted hosting.** Cloud Run's A2A deploy doc defaults to `--no-allow-unauthenticated` (IAM-gated) and documents `--allow-unauthenticated` with card-level `securitySchemes`/`security` for public agents (GDK `search_documents`, 2026-10-08) — relevant if the arena hosts its own candidates on Cloud Run, less relevant if an entrant hosts their own endpoint (then the arena is simply an A2A *client* calling out, and the entrant's own hosting choices are out of scope).

## Q3. Per-hop A2A latency vs. the 3-second coaching budget (KPI-4)

**No reproducible, independently measured number was found** in this batch either, matching X4's unresolved open question five days later. What was found:

- "Google ADK A2A delivers 32% lower latency and 63% higher throughput than LangGraph A2A middleware, and 57% less memory per connection" and "an A2A Proxy adding 8ms at p95" (web search, 2026, vendor/blog-style sources, no stated methodology or infra details reached). **Low confidence** — no methodology, no independent corroboration, reads as marketing framing.
- "Streaming reduces perceived latency by 40% for LLM-heavy workloads" (web search synthesis, 2026). **Low confidence**, same reason.
- A pilot academic benchmark, arXiv 2603.22823 ("systematic pilot benchmark comparing tool integration, multi-agent delegation, and hybrid architectures," v3 dated 2026-04-23, fetched via WebFetch) tracks response time, context consumption, cost, error recovery, and implementation complexity as metrics — but its abstract does not name A2A or MCP specifically, and the full PDF's binary stream could not be decoded by WebFetch this session (would need a proper PDF-to-text pull, e.g. `pdftotext`, outside this tool's reach). **Low confidence / inconclusive** — flagged as a lead worth a direct follow-up, not as evidence.
- One explicit, useful fact: A2A protocol latency is defined as covering "negotiation, authentication, skill discovery, tool selection, and result serialization" end to end, and pre-flight capability negotiation per request adds extra round trips unless cached (web search, 2026, `gravitee.io` corpus page). This at least names where overhead would come from (card fetch/negotiation is cacheable after the first call; JSON serialization and TLS/HTTP handshake are the recurring per-call costs) even without a number attached. **Low-medium confidence** — plausible and consistent with how HTTP/JSON-RPC generally behaves, but the source itself reads as a vendor content page, not a primary spec or measurement.

**Reasoned inference (not sourced, explicitly flagged as such):** in a single-region Cloud Run deployment, warm-instance round-trip cost for a small JSON-RPC payload is very likely a small fraction of a 3-second budget (tens of milliseconds), but **Cloud Run cold start on a scale-to-zero candidate is the real risk to KPI-4**, not steady-state protocol overhead — a candidate that has scaled to zero between turns could blow the 3-second budget on cold start alone, independent of A2A. No source measured this directly for an A2A-wrapped ADK agent; it is general Cloud Run knowledge applied to this specific risk. **Low-medium confidence**, flagged as an open question requiring a hands-on timed smoke test before relying on any number from this research.

## Q4. ADK `to_a2a`/`RemoteA2aAgent` and Cloud Run's A2A deploy path (Preview)

Unchanged from X4: `to_a2a(agent, port=...)` exposes an ADK agent as a Starlette A2A server with an auto-built card; `RemoteA2aAgent(agent_card=URL)` consumes one; SDK major version (0.3.x vs 1.x) is auto-detected. **New this session:** `A2aRemoteAgentConfig` with `CardRequestInterceptor`/`RequestInterceptor` hooks (Q1/Q2 above) is the concrete auth-injection mechanism — this closes a gap X4 left open. **High confidence**, primary SDK docs.

Cloud Run's deploy path (GDK, `docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/deploy-a2a-agents`, 2026-10-08): `gcloud run deploy ... --functional-type=agent --identity-type=agent-identity` auto-registers the service in Agent Registry with a system-managed Agent Identity; task storage is either **in-memory** (lost on scale-to-zero/restart — acceptable for the arena's 1-2-user, stateless-turn use case) or **AlloyDB for PostgreSQL** (persistent, for horizontal scale — not needed here). Default auth is `--no-allow-unauthenticated` (IAM); public agents need `--allow-unauthenticated` plus card-level `securitySchemes`. Required IAM roles are broad: Cloud Run Source Developer, Project IAM Admin, Secret Manager Admin, Service Account User, Secret Manager Secret Accessor, Vertex AI User — heavier than D-003's "simple architecture" default `gcloud run deploy --source .` flow. **High confidence**, primary docs, but **flagged against D-003** as a complexity/least-privilege tension worth a deliberate decision rather than copy-paste.

**Gotcha directly relevant to the scale-to-zero hard gate:** a *different* Google sample (CX Agent Studio's Cloud Run deploy snippet for an ADK agent, GDK `search_documents`, 2026-10-08) uses `gcloud run deploy ... --no-cpu-throttling` — i.e., CPU-always-allocated — for an A2A-exposed agent. The A2A-specific deploy doc's own command examples (above) do **not** include that flag. **This is a direct, sourced contradiction inside Google's own documentation, and a landmine**: if anyone copies the CX Agent Studio sample instead of the plain A2A deploy doc, it silently sets `--no-cpu-throttling`, which the owner's hard gate forbids outright. **High confidence this flag appears in an official sample this session; high confidence it would violate the gate if copied.**

A second, already-known-from-X4 gotcha reconfirmed via GDK this session: the *Vertex AI Agent Engine* deploy path (separate from Cloud Run) sets `"min_instances": 1` in its own sample `agent_config` dict (GDK `search_documents`, 2026-10-08) — Agent Engine's own tooling defaults away from scale-to-zero, again. Cloud Run (without `--no-cpu-throttling`) remains the safer default of the two Google-provided A2A hosting paths.

## Q5. Tracing A2A hops into Phoenix without an OpenInference A2A instrumentor

Reconfirmed: `openinference-instrumentation-a2a` does not exist on PyPI (X4, unchanged). W3C `traceparent` is the mechanism to hand-roll manual spans (GDK, `docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/trace-context`, 2026-10-08): format `00-TRACE_ID-PARENT_SPAN_ID-TRACE_FLAGS`, and "Google Cloud services that support trace context propagation typically support both the traceparent and the legacy X-Cloud-Trace-Context header," with traceparent preferred. Since A2A's JSON-RPC-over-HTTP transport is ordinary HTTP, injecting a `traceparent` header on the outbound A2A request is just standard header injection — no protocol extension needed. Concrete recipe implied by the sources: (1) start/continue an OTel span client-side before calling `client.send_message(...)`, inject the active context as a `traceparent` header on the HTTP call; (2) if the remote agent is our own ADK instance, extract that header and feed it to ADK's own `maybe_set_otel_providers()`/`invoke_agent` span so child spans nest correctly (X4); (3) if the remote agent is an untrusted BYO entrant, there is no guarantee it propagates or honors `traceparent` at all — the trace simply terminates at the host's own outbound span, which is actually sufficient for the arena's purposes (it needs "how long did the black box take and what did it return," not the entrant's internals). Phoenix ingests whatever OTel/OTLP spans arrive regardless of who authored them, so a hand-written `a2a.call` span (attributes: `a2a.task_id`, `a2a.agent_card.url`, `a2a.message_id`, HTTP status) wrapping each `send_message`/streaming call is sufficient, consistent with X4's implication that this is scoped manual-instrumentation work, not missing infrastructure. **High confidence** on the mechanism; **medium confidence** that it composes cleanly with Phoenix's existing session/trace model specifically for A2A (not independently tested this session, carried as an implication from the general OTel/Phoenix pattern).

## Q6. Precedents: public competitions accepting A2A submissions

**AgentBeats / AgentX** (UC Berkeley RDI, Phase 1 running 2025-10-16 to 2026-01-31, Phase 2 from 2026-03-02; web search, 2026) is a close, concrete precedent: a "green agent" (evaluator/benchmark host) opens an A2A task and relays addresses/config to "purple agents" (entrants); entrants need only "expose their agent as an A2A server" in any language to compete, across tracks including Agent Safety, Research Agent, Multi-agent Evaluation, and others. A companion paper, *"AgentBeats: Agentifying Agent Assessment for Openness, Standardization, and Reproducibility,"* was found only via a secondary abstract mirror (`fugumt.com`, 2026) — the canonical arXiv ID was not directly confirmed this session. **Medium confidence** on the overall design (corroborated across the official site and the paper abstract mirror); **low confidence / open question** on exact paper citation details.

**Counter-precedent, already in hand:** TechnoMile's own `docs/research/swarm/A2A.md` (2026-10-03, read per instructions) explicitly **rejected** real A2A transport for its competitive multi-agent swarm, choosing "A2A-shaped types over an in-process bus" instead — reasons given: ~25 extra local ports per run, a banned ADK-orchestration dependency under its own SPEC (`REQ-RUN-18`), and research that cross-agent chatter causes conformity rather than useful signal in agent ensembles (their H6 citation). This is directly relevant contradicting evidence: **one real project in the same owner's portfolio chose not to use real A2A transport for competitive agents**, for reasons (deploy surface, dependency bans) that partly overlap with this arena's own "simple architecture, scale to zero" constraint (D-003) — though TechnoMile's scenario was a single-team internal swarm, not a cross-org BYO bake-off, so the two cases are not fully analogous. **High confidence** this precedent exists and says what it says (primary internal doc); **no claim** about whether its reasoning transfers to this arena.

No other named public competition with a confirmed A2A-specific submission protocol was found this session (Colosseum Agent Hackathon, CrowdStrike AgentWorks, Claw-a-thon, Brown's SCML all surfaced in search results but none showed a confirmed A2A submission mechanism in the snippets reached) — **not counted as precedents**, listed only to show they were checked and excluded.

## Contradictions

1. **Agent Card "v1.0" schema shape disagrees across two Google-adjacent sources.** The `a2a-python` proto (Context7) uses `additional_interfaces`/`preferred_transport`/`security_schemes`/`signatures`. Google Cloud's own Agent Registry docs (GDK, `docs.cloud.google.com/agent-registry/json-schemas`, 2026-10-08) describe a **different** "Version 1.0 schema (recommended)" using `supportedInterfaces[{url, protocolBinding, protocolVersion, tenant}]` and `capabilities.extendedAgentCard`, citing `github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/v1.0.1/...` — a *different* version tag (v1.0.1) than X4's "frozen 2026-03-12" v1.0. Unreconciled; carried over from X4, now reconfirmed from a second independent Google source rather than resolved.
2. **Cloud Run deploy guidance disagrees on CPU allocation for A2A agents.** The A2A-specific Cloud Run deploy doc's own example commands do not set `--no-cpu-throttling`; a separate Google sample (CX Agent Studio's Cloud Run deploy snippet for an ADK/A2A agent) does. Directly load-bearing for this project's hard scale-to-zero gate.
3. **Latency claims are mutually uncorroborated.** "32% lower latency than LangGraph," "8ms p95 proxy overhead," and "40% perceived-latency reduction from streaming" come from three different sources with no shared methodology, infra, or region stated — none can be used as an input to the KPI-4 budget decision.
4. **mTLS for A2A auth was asked for but not found.** Either it is out-of-SDK-scope (handled at the ingress/transport layer) or this session's sources simply didn't surface it — treated as an open question, not resolved either way.

## Open questions

- Exact arXiv ID and full text of the AgentBeats paper (only a secondary mirror abstract was reached).
- A real, reproducible single-region Cloud Run A2A per-hop latency measurement — absent after two research passes five days apart.
- Whether A2A's `SecurityScheme` model can express mTLS at all, or whether mTLS for this arena would have to be a Cloud Run ingress/load-balancer concern outside the SDK.
- Whether the Cloud Run A2A deploy path's broader IAM role list is acceptable under D-003's "simple architecture" or should be trimmed/justified explicitly.
- Whether `a2a-inspector` or `adk conformance test` can be scripted into an automated pre-flight CI gate for an entrant, versus being purely human-driven debugging tools (not confirmed either way this session).
- Whether the full text of arXiv 2603.22823 (once properly parsed) contains a usable A2A-specific timing number — this session's WebFetch could not decode the PDF stream.
- Whether AgentBeats' actual orchestration code (not just its paper/site description) is public and worth reading directly for interviewer-harness design ideas.

## Implications for the build (no recommendation)

- AST-7's schema-enforced flag (cited turn + closed category enum) maps directly onto an A2A `DataPart` JSON object; host-side validation against the arena's own schema is mandatory regardless of transport — A2A supplies the carrier, not the guarantee.
- BKO-5's "equal budgets" (turn cap, max tokens, context limit, response budget) has no A2A-native support and must be enforced entirely at the harness layer — identical engineering effort whether or not A2A is adopted, so A2A-vs-in-process is not a shortcut on this requirement.
- SCN-9 isolation reduces to one serialization-boundary function building the outbound Message/DataPart from only the public+subject packets, never the evaluator-only packet — a natural, narrow unit-test surface.
- Real A2A transport for BYO entrants looks closer to turnkey than the TechnoMile precedent's objections assumed (Cloud Run's Preview A2A deploy path, `to_a2a`/`RemoteA2aAgent`, and the newly-found `CardRequestInterceptor`/`RequestInterceptor` auth hooks address the "needs servers + a new dependency + no auth story" concerns) — but TechnoMile's rejection was for a non-adversarial, single-team internal swarm, not a cross-org bake-off, so its conclusion doesn't automatically transfer either way.
- Given the total absence of a trustworthy A2A per-hop latency number against a 3-second KPI, a short timed smoke test (one real Cloud Run round trip, cold and warm) is the only way to know whether A2A overhead is negligible or a material bite out of the budget before committing to wrapping every candidate in A2A.
- Observability requires hand-written OTel spans with manual `traceparent` header injection around every A2A client call, since no OpenInference A2A instrumentor exists — scoped, bounded engineering work, not missing infrastructure, and it degrades gracefully against an opaque BYO entrant that doesn't propagate the header back.
- AgentBeats/AgentX is close enough as a real precedent (green/purple agents over A2A) to be worth a direct read of its public harness design before building this arena's own interviewer-harness/bake-off runner, so as not to re-derive already-solved orchestration problems.
- Any Cloud Run A2A deploy script written for this project must be hand-checked against the `--no-cpu-throttling` and Agent-Engine-style `min_instances` anti-patterns found in Google's own sample code this session, before it goes anywhere near the Pre-Push Quality Bar / scale-to-zero audit.
